title: mut.channel_saraceno_spider_web_tomography
mutation_directive: Tomás Saraceno — Spider Web Scan / Hybrid Webs — How to entangle the universe in a spider web? (TBA21, Vienna 2018); ongoing 3D laser-scanned spider-web archive (only one in existence). VISUAL SIGNATURE: Sparse luminous filaments suspended in pitch black — irregular, non-grid, knot-like clusters connected by long thin strands. Spider-web tomography: real arachnid architecture digitized as point + line cloud. Faintly metallic / pearlescent thread on cosmic black; reads as both biological and astronomical. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: Generate a 3D Delaunay-like sparse graph: ~300 anchor nodes in a bounded volume, connect each to its 2–4 nearest with probability falling off in distance, then add a few long-range 'guy-line' threads. Render edges as thin GL_LINES with additive bloom; nodes as tiny sprites. Slowly perturb anchor positions by a soft spring + light wind field — the whole web breathes. Stereoscopic camera dolly to let viewer 'walk through' as Saraceno's scans intend. WHY DIVERSE: Pool's webs (Shiota red-yarn) are dense, painterly, color-saturated. This is the opposite register: scientific, sparse, achromatic, single-organism architecture. And it's a graph, not a cloud — connectivity matters. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://studiotomassaraceno.org/2-dimensional_webs_archivemaps_and_traces/
